finding.claim: SQL injection in /search: the unauthenticated q parameter is interpolated into an f-string SQL query with no escaping or parameter binding, allowing UNION-based reads of arbitrary tables in shop.db.
finding.sink: app.py:12 db.execute(f"SELECT id, name FROM products WHERE name LIKE '%{term}%'")

trace.note: Route /search is unauthenticated; no auth decorator or middleware exists in the app
term taken directly from request query string
term interpolated into SQL text via f-string; no validation, escaping, or ? binding
fetchall() result returned to client as JSON, so injected UNION results are visible

finding.guards_checked: No validation, sanitizer, allowlist, escaping, or parameterized binding on the path. sqlite3 execute() allows only a single statement, so stacked DML is blocked, but UNION-based SELECT injection is not. Other sinks checked: /product/<int:pid> (app.py:18) and /by-owner (app.py:25) use ? binding and are SAFE; no subprocess, eval, deserialization, template, outbound request, file path, or secret sinks exist in the repo.

verdict.guard_found: none. /search (app.py:9) has no auth decorator or middleware, so the attacker is anonymous. q is read raw at app.py:11 and f-string interpolated into SQL at app.py:12 with no escaping, allowlist, or ? binding. The rows are returned via jsonify at app.py:13, so UNION results are visible. sqlite3's single-statement limit blocks stacked DML but not UNION SELECT. The other routes (app.py:18, app.py:25) use ? binding and are not affected.
verdict.reason: The trace matches app.py:9-13: /search is unauthenticated, app.py:11 takes q from the request, app.py:12 interpolates it into SQL via f-string with no guard, and app.py:13 returns the fetchall() rows to the client, so a UNION-based SQL injection read is reachable and unblocked.
